sources.title: Flipkart Careers - How We Hire
sources.basis: Flipkart's own careers page describing its hiring process
sources.summary: Seven-step process: application, application assessment, optional technical phone screen, onsite interview (recruiter explains number of rounds), independent hiring committee review of interviewer feedback, offer rollout, joining; plus an FAQ. Not role-specific; no questions.

sources.title: Flipkart Interview Experience for SDE-2
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: May 2024 SDE-2 loop (offer): 2.5h machine coding (30 min brief / 90 min coding / 30 min review) building a wallet system; DSA round with Longest Valid Parentheses and Maximum Performance of a Team; design round 'design a Jukebox/Spotify' (APIs, schema, DB indexing); hiring manager round.

sources.title: My Interview Experience at Flipkart for SDE 2
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-2 loop: machine coding a demoable stock-market app (tracking, orders, portfolio) with a code-review session three days later; DSA round with 'burning tree' and 'buy/sell stock with at most k transactions'; LLD-style design of Apple Health (schema expected); managerial round; a second design round (transport management) after re-evaluation.

sources.title: Flipkart SDE-2 Interview Experience
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-2 backend hiring drive: four rounds (machine coding, DSA, design, hiring manager). Machine coding over a shared Google Meet with ~30 candidates: build an investing app (add user/stock, buy, sell, view portfolio, admin-controlled prices), 30/90/30 min brief/code/review; DSA two mediums (string, recursion/DP); HLD 'design a Spotify service' with search optimisation.

sources.title: Flipkart Machine Coding Interview Experience
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: In-person machine coding round (rejected): candidates briefed together by a senior engineer, 1.5h to code an order notification service with stakeholders, role-based users and a bonus part, followed by a panel discussion of the implementation; author's reflections on time allocation.

sources.title: Cracking the Flipkart SDE-1 Interview: My Journey and Insights
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-1 loop: machine coding a bowling alley scorer (strikes, spares, bonus) judged on demoable code, readability, patterns, exception handling; DSA round with Set Matrix Zeroes and Car Pooling in one hour; managerial round on current architecture and motivation.

sources.title: Swiggy Interview Experience for SDE 2 Backend Developer
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-2 backend loop (offer, OA skipped): DSA round with two Swiggy-framed problems similar to Word Break and Partition Array for Maximum Sum; 1h LLD round coding a Top-K restaurant discovery system (nearest, nearest available, 50% discount, highest rated); HM round with HLD of splitting one pharma+grocery order into child orders under a parentOrderId (concurrency, sibling lookup); a second HM round for team matching.

sources.title: Swiggy SDE-1 (Backend) | Interview Experience | 1+ years of Experience
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-1 Go backend loop (rejected after last round): HackerRank OA in Go (3 questions); 1h technical round with Reverse String (warm-up) and Gas Station; 75-min LLD/machine coding round (five-part problem, statement linked as a Google Doc, not reproduced in the post); engineering-manager round on past projects.

sources.title: Swiggy Interview Experience Backend Position
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: Associate SDE backend loop (selected, Feb 2024): OA with CS fundamentals, one easy DSA and one API-response backend question; LLD round coding a game problem judged on SOLID/OOP/readability; LLD+HLD round reviewing that code then designing APIs and schema for a live Swiggy Instamart feature; hiring manager round (Kafka, RabbitMQ, projects).

sources.title: Swiggy SDE-1 (Backend) | Interview Experience | [Offer]
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: New-grad SDE-1 backend loop (offer; older than three years): OA of 3 questions; DSA round with Maximum Length of Pair Chain and longest valid substring; machine coding round 'design Splitwise' with five features and scale trade-offs; hiring manager round on projects and behavioural questions.

sources.title: Beyond Resumes: Setting A-Teams through Values-Driven Interviews
sources.basis: Razorpay's own company blog, authored by its Culture Head, describing how interviews are structured
sources.summary: Describes Razorpay's values-based interview approach: interviewers probe six named values (Customer First, Autonomy & Ownership, Challenging the Status Quo, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Razorpay Grows with Razors) by asking for specific examples rather than assessing resumes/credentials alone. Not engineering-specific and no named questions.

sources.title: My FrontEnd Interview Experience At Razorpay
sources.basis: The author's own free dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: Frontend engineer loop, four rounds: 1h technical deep-dive on past projects/design-system work; 1.5h pair-programming coding round on CodeSandbox (any framework); 1h open-ended web-fundamentals discussion; 1h hiring-manager culture-fit round. Older than three years but specific and first-hand.

sources.title: CRED Interview Experience
sources.basis: The author's own personal blog (GitHub Pages), cited and linked
sources.summary: Frontend Developer loop (offer), interviewed July 2021: three 90-minute technical rounds (JS problem with live optimisation discussion; machine coding a search box with API integration covering event delegation, defer/async, module patterns, virtual DOM, Next.js routing; React machine coding building a PAN/Aadhaar form-validation app), a 60-minute cultural-fit round, then salary discussion.

sources.title: How (and Why) Postman Created a Data-Driven Hiring Process
sources.basis: Postman's own company blog describing its hiring process design
sources.summary: Describes Postman's hiring funnel (Applied, Screening, Technical Interview, Interviews, Offer, Hired) grouped into Attract/Screen/Interview/Offer phases, service-level objectives per stage (e.g. candidates not left in 'Applied' more than a day), automated candidate communication, and metrics tracked (time-to-hire, Process Performance Score, Candidate Experience Score). Not engineering-specific; no named questions.

sources.title: How to be Successful Interviewing for Big Tech
sources.basis: Postman's own company blog, written by the Postman engineer (Codegen team lead) who designed the process being described
sources.summary: Postman engineering lead describes the three-stage engineering interview he built at Postman: a take-home task with paired code review, a system-design conversation focused on trade-offs, and a behavioural/culture-fit round. States candidates may use AI tools, search engines, and modern tooling during interviews because 'the interview should mirror the job.'

sources.title: My Interview Experience for Senior Software Engineer Role at Walmart Global Tech
sources.basis: The author's own free dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: Senior Software Engineer loop, completed in one week (October 2025), four rounds: DSA (binary tree level-order traversal, DFS graph traversal plus a follow-up); LLD designing a Restaurant Reservation and Serving System (Spring Boot, transactions, ACID); HLD with a Java multithreading warm-up (print numbers using three threads in sequence) then 'design a video streaming system like Netflix or Disney+ Hotstar' (bitrates, CDNs, DB scalability); hiring-manager round on projects and ownership. Candidate received the offer.

sources.title: Goldman Sachs SDE-1 Interview Experience (2024)
sources.basis: The author's own free dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-1 interview (candidate not selected): reproduces two coding questions actually asked with the author's Java attempts - a 'shortest subarray with sum at least k' problem and a minimum-sum grid path (DP) problem. Thin on round structure; strong on two named, verifiable questions.

gaps: Systemic issue this session: medium.com (including custom-domain Medium publications like engineering.razorpay.com) returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch on every attempt after the first few minutes of this run, most likely because several sibling research agents in the same overnight run were fetching Medium concurrently and triggered rate-limiting/bot-blocking. Medium is the dominant venue for individual authors' interview-experience posts about Indian product companies, so this materially reduced what could be verified for: Zomato, Zerodha, Freshworks, Zoho, Meesho, PhonePe, Paytm, Myntra, JPMorgan Chase, BrowserStack, Uber India, Ola, InMobi. Many strong-looking free Medium candidates were found by search (e.g. multiple Zomato SDE posts, PhonePe frontend/backend posts, Paytm senior-SE posts, Ola/InMobi/Myntra SDE posts) but were NOT recorded because they could not be fetched and confirmed this session. Recommend a follow-up pass once Medium access is available again - search queries used are listed per company below.
